OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri K. Gopalan, a former Member and Shri Vasant Chavan, 
a sitting Member of this House. 
Shri K. Gopalan passed away on the 9th June, 2006, at the age of 87 
years. Born at Calicut in+ Kerala in  December, 1919, Shri Gopalan had his 
education at Malabar Christian Colleg e, Calicut and St. Thomas College, 
Triohur. 
A journalist and a social worker, Shri Gopalan participated in the 
freedom struggle. Shri Gopalan was associated with literary and cultural 
activities and library movements in Kerala. He was editor of several 
magazines and dailies and also wrote poems and articles in local 
publications. 
Shri Gopalan was a Member of the Madras Legislative Council. He 
represented the State of Kerala in this House from July, 1982 to July, 1988. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [24 July, 2006] 
In the passing away of Shri G opalan, the country has lost a noted 
social worker. 
Shri Vasant Chavan passed away on the 11th July, 2006 at the age of 
64 years following cardiac arrest. Born at Deolali Camp, Nasik in Maharashtra 
in 1942, Shri Chavan had his education at the University of Pune, 
Maharashtra. A Sanskrit scholar, Shri Chavan stood first in Senior School 
Certificate Examination in the year 1962 and was awarded a Gold Medal in 
Sanskrit. 
A political and social worker, Shri Chavan was associated with 
various social, welfare and educational institutions. He was the President of 
Antyodaya Parishad, Maharashtra. The long and distinguished political career 
of Shri Chavan started with the mem bership of the Maharashtra Legislative 
Assembly where he was Member from 1980 to 1985. Thereafter, in 1985 itself 
he was elected to the Maharashtra Legislative Council and remained a 
Member of the Council till 2004. He also  had the distinction of serving as a 
Minister in the Government of Maharashtra and held portfolios of Urban 
Development, Law and Justice, Food and Civil Supply between 1992 and 
1994. Again, between 1999 and 2001, he served as Minister of Excise and, 
Food and Drugs Administration in the Government of Maharashtra. 
Shri Chavan represented the Stat e of Maharashtra in this House 
from April, 2005 to April, 2006 and, agai n, from April, 2006 till his sad demise. 
Shri Chavan visited UK to attend the Commonwealth Parliamentary 
Conference in the year 1993. 
In the passing away of Shri Vasant Chavan, the country has lost a 
noted Parliamentarian, a dedicated social worker and an able administrator. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri K. Gopalan and Shri Vasant 
Chavan. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence for one 
minute as a mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General wi ll convey to the members of 
the bereaved families our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy.

REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR 
References to the victims of earthquake and tsunami in Java Island of 
Indonesia and serial bomb blasts in Mumbai and terrorist attacks In Srinagar, 
Jammu and Kashmir 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as  you are aware, an earthquake 
measuring 6.3 on Richter scale stru ck Indonesia's Java Island on the 27 th 
May, 2006, causing large scale devastation. 
The Island was struck again by a Tsunami, caused by a massive 
undersea earthquake of 7.7 magnit ude on the Richter scale on the 17 th July, 
2006, reportedly killing more than 50 0 persons and affecting thousands of 
others. 
The House expresses its heartfelt sympathy and condolences to the 
people of Indonesia who have lost their near and dear ones in these tragedies 
and pray for the early recovery of those who were injured. 
Hon. Members, as you are alread y aware, 184 persons were killed 
and more than 840 persons got injured in the serial bomb blasts that took 
place in the suburban trains of Mumbai on the 11 th July, 2006. Further, 9 
persons were also reportedly killed and 33 persons got injured in a series of 
grenade attacks, targeted at tourists, the same day, in Srinagar, Jammu and 
Kashmir. 
The killing of so many innocent persons has shocked the entire nation. 
Those who intend to harm this nation and destabilise our society will never 
succeed in their evil designs. Their despicable acts can be neutralised by our 
people by showing unity and will to resist. We have seen how in times of 
distress, our nation has stood united. I am  sure that the whole House will join 
me in pondemning these brutal and senseless aots of terrorism. We resolve to 
fight terrorism unitedly and with determination. We offer condolences to the 
bereaved families and pray for early recovery of those who got  Injured in 
these blasts. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark 
of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
